subject: Live endpoint: sustained stream-drip and chunk timeouts — urgent
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@bluehaven.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-03T08:15:22-08:00
Subject: Re: live endpoint — intermittent stream stalls and 503s

Kimberly —

We started seeing a clear pattern this morning on our production route (v2/live). During bursts, the token stream is delivering a handful of chunks and then goes quiet for 12–30s before either resuming or returning a 502/504. Throughput is down ~40% on peak traffic and our client-side retries are spiking error rates.

Attached is a small capture (session_dump_1103.txt) and a short timeline of sample requests. We’re running against the hosted endpoint in us-west and haven’t changed any client-side keepalives.

Immediate ask: can you confirm whether this is a networking/proxy issue or something in the runtime’s chunk coalescing? We’ve opened an incident internally but wanted to loop you in — this is impacting a customer-facing billing-run.

Thanks — appreciate any immediate mitigation.

— Alex
Ops Lead, Bluehaven
ops@bluehaven.com

Alex —

Thanks for the quick capture and for flagging. I’m escalating this to SRE and runtime engineering immediately. Short answers up front: we see correlated spikes in streaming latency and a small increase in 5xx on that route; we’ve created INF-1289 to track.

Short-term mitigations we can push right away (will enact after confirming with SRE):
- Toggle shorter keepalive (30s -> 10s) on the proxy layer for the affected pool.
- Route heavy sessions to a dedicated pool with smaller max_chunk_size to reduce coalescing pressure.
- Enable temporary 429 backpressure to smooth bursts while we triage.

Can you confirm whether Bluehaven can tolerate a 2-hour maintenance window this morning for a targeted configuration change? If yes I’ll coordinate and share a playbook.

I’ve attached a snapshot of the SLO dashboard we pulled (slo_snapshot_1103.png). I’ll follow up with proposed rollback criteria.

On Wed, Nov 3, 2026 at 8:15 AM Alex Turner <alex.turner@bluehaven.com> wrote:
> Kimberly —
>
> We started seeing a clear pattern this morning on our production route (v2/live)...

My initial read: the pattern lines up with an observable proxy behavior where chunk coalescing can produce a long tail if the client or proxy buffers until a threshold is hit. At high concurrency, the runtime can end up holding a partial KV cache flush while waiting for an input boundary; that shows up as a quiet window and then a burst/timeout.

Immediate actions I recommend we take concurrently:
1) Apply the shorter TCP keepalive at the proxy (as Kimberly suggested).
2) Drop max_chunk_size on the live pool from 16KB -> 6KB for the next 2 hours.
3) Enable connection-level streaming debug logging for a 15-minute window and stream the logs to the incident channel.
4) If we see no improvement in 30 minutes, failover route to a smaller quantized model that has lower per-request memory pressure.

I’ve pushed a minimal config to the staging control plane and will promote to production if we get go-ahead. Tracking: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INF-1289

— Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

Subject: SUMMARY / ask: Bluehaven live-route streaming degradation (INF-1289)

Folks — summary and request for exec approval. Thread INF-1289 has tracked a high-priority customer escalation from Bluehaven (see timeline below). We mitigated the immediate customer pain with a targeted config change on 2026-11-03 but have not yet proven the long-term fix.

Timeline (short):
- 11/03 08:15 PT: Bluehaven reports intermittent streaming quiet windows and 5xx spikes (see session dump).
- 11/03 09:00 PT: We apply proxy keepalive reduction and lower max_chunk_size; observed immediate ~60% reduction in quiet-window frequency.
- 11/03 09:30 PT: War room established; 30m observation window shows improved throughput but a small increase in average CPU on the pool.
- 11/04–11/05: Continued monitoring; background root-cause points to the proxy’s coalescing heuristics interacting poorly with some client TCP stacks under bursty concurrency.

Current status: customer is stable on the mitigated route but we should implement a durable fix in the next sprint: either adjust the coalescing threshold in the proxy (preferred) or introduce a runtime guard that preemptively flushes partial chunks after a short timeout. Engineering estimate: 2–4 engineer-days including testing.

Ask (exec approval):
1) Approve a 2-hour targeted production maintenance window to deploy the proxy coalescing threshold fix and validate (we plan to do a canary first).
2) Approve offering Bluehaven a 20% service credit for the impacted billing window if the root-cause confirms our proxy bug.
3) Approve priority engineering allocation (2 engineer-days) to deliver the durable fix in the next sprint rather than backlog.

Attachments: remediation_steps.md, customer_impact_summary.pdf

I recommend approval for the maintenance window and the credit so we can close the incident with the customer safely. I’ll coordinate communications if we have sign-off.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
